title: Panner: A Low-Cost, High-Recall Pre-Screening Module for Systematic Reviews
content: Before a model can screen a citation, the review team must decide what satisfies each eligibility criterion and which combinations of findings justify exclusion. PANNER makes these decisions explicit through interactive protocol compilation. A host agent works with the team to turn the criteria into atomic signal questions, answer conditions and rules for combining the answers. After the team reviews and freezes the protocol, a calibrated decision model answers the questions for each citation, and a fixed rule engine derives the retain or exclude decision. Records are retained for further assessment whenever no exclusion rule is satisfied. Implemented as a local Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, PANNER preserves the source criteria, protocols, answers and run configurations for inspection and recomputation. In four worked examples, it screened 26,195 deduplicated citations and excluded 21,768 (83.1%), leaving 4,427 for downstream screening. All 67 supplied reference reports were retained; these records also informed protocol calibration. Jev screening cost US$3.39, with approximately US$0.54 in estimated agent compilation costs. The examples illustrate how an explicit screening protocol can guide inexpensive batch judgements and reduce the number of records requiring further assessment.
